title: Machine Learning Metabolomics Profiling of Dietary Interventions from a Six-Week Randomised Trial
summary: In a six-week randomized dietary intervention involving 64 healthy adults, elastic-net analysis prioritized serum and stool metabolites that distinguished inulin and omega-3 intervention arms. The metabolite findings are exploratory and do not establish longer-term health effects.
ai_technology: Elastic-net feature selection identified metabolite changes discriminating the randomized inulin and omega-3 arms; Random Forest and logistic regression were used as sensitivity checks and to assess microbiome contributions.
organization: University of Minnesota; University of California, Davis

source_review.scope: Primary full text, including Methods and Results; primary publication record or first result-bearing version checked.

evidence.tested: Repeated cross-validation and sensitivity analyses assessed metabolite discrimination; selected changes were also examined within intervention arms.
evidence.unknown: Small, short-duration trial; metabolite discrimination does not establish clinical benefit or persistent biological effects.
evidence.ai_role: Elastic-net feature selection identified metabolite changes discriminating the randomized inulin and omega-3 arms; Random Forest and logistic regression were used as sensitivity checks and to assess microbiome contributions.
